title: Rebuilt Buildings in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Central Berlin looks older than it is.** Of the fourteen landmarks between the Staatsoper and Alexanderplatz, only four are still the material they were originally built from.

**St. Mary's Church is the real medieval survivor.** Brick walls from around 1270, standing through the war because Allied bomber crews used it as a navigation landmark. The pointed spire on top is neo-Gothic, added by Carl Gotthard Langhans in 1789.

**The Humboldt Forum and the Nikolaiviertel are reconstructions.** The royal palace was blown up in 1950 and the current building went up between 2013 and 2020. The Nikolaiviertel was built from prefabricated concrete between 1981 and 1987.

**Several landmarks are rebuilds behind their original design.** The Rotes Rathaus was rebuilt to the 1860s drawings between 1951 and 1956, the Zeughaus between 1948 and 1965, the Staatsoper between 1951 and 1955.

**The Berliner Dom lost sixteen metres.** After the 1944 fire, the reconstruction from 1975 to 1993 brought the dome and the four corner towers back lower than before, and the Memorial Church wing was never rebuilt.
**Go to the Neues Museum if you want to see the join.** David Chipperfield's restoration, finished in 2009, left shell holes and scorched brick visible against plainly new surfaces.

**Four checks tell you almost everything:** follow the brick upward for the line where old meets new, look for repeated house types, look for two ages of carving on one wall, and look for the deliberate modern break a good reconstruction always admits to.
